entry_conditions: Drawer is open/stable; observations and measured joints are valid; the block is plausibly attached for carry entry or visibly in the cavity/release corridor for mid-skill entry; the state is not an unseen drop recovery.
exit_conditions: Causal geometry indicates a stationary drawer-floor-height block detached from TCP; TCP has retreated and preferably reached the handle approach for close_drawer.
overlap_role: Every 680:1160 action is supervised. The 680:840 retrieval overlap admits predecessor intermediate states; 900:1160 explicitly covers opening, variable settling holds, retreat, reorientation, handle approach and re-closing.
successor_readiness: Transfer to close_drawer only when actual object height and two-frame motion support deposited-retreat or handle-ready. The auxiliary class alone is insufficient. Keep two causal frames across the switch.
failure_signatures: Predicted phase conflicts with object/TCP motion; object stops following before intended release; opening occurs outside the cavity; object continues following after opening; local increments repeatedly grow or drift; or IK reports nonconvergence/limits.
continuation_guidance: Use this policy for locally perturbed or phase-ambiguous states near demonstrated geometry. Switch to place_block_in_drawer__h01 for a largely displaced plausibly attached block, or place_block_in_drawer__h02 for a displaced destination and fixture-anchored post-release motion.
limitations: The four phase labels are coarse and derived from successful demonstration geometry/actions, not simulator contact. Current-TCP increments do not establish global displacement robustness and may accumulate error. No demonstration supports recovery from a dropped object.
